summary: Melissa R. Kerin works in art history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter, and was attested as a professor at Washington and Lee University in 2015.

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology and anthropology. He studied at the University of Michigan (BA ~1955–1959) and the University of Washington (PhD ~1960–1968), and spent his career at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002) as a professor of anthropology.

Merab Mamardashvili was a philosopher who studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (~1949–1954). He later held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).

Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell and completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1980).
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.

Michael Alram is a numismatist and historian who studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the University of Vienna, and the Kunsthistorisches Museum, including Coin Cabinet director (2008–2020).

Michael Aris was a scholar of Tibetology and history. He studied at Durham University and earned his PhD at SOAS under David Llewellyn Snellgrove, later holding academic posts at Oxford, including Wolfson College, St Antony's, and Harvard.

Michael Balk is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1988 and held an attested post at the Prussian State Library in 1991.

Michael Baxandall was an art historian educated at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, the Courtauld Institute of Art, the University of California, Berkeley, and Cornell University.
Michael Bernays was a scholar who studied at Bonn and Heidelberg under Adolf Holtzmann. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).

Michael Carrithers is an anthropologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Oxford, later lecturing at Oxford and the LSE before serving as Professor of Anthropology at Durham University (appointed lecturer 1982).

Michael Chase is a scholar of ancient philosophy. He studied at the University of Victoria and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (PhD by 2000), later holding research posts at the CNRS (2001–2009) and Centre Jean Pépin (2009).

Michael Comans specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University (~1983–1987), and served on the faculty at the University of Sydney.
Michael Como is a scholar of Japanese religions and Buddhist studies who studied under Bernard Faure, Carl Bielefeldt, and Kuo-liang Wang. He held an attested post at Columbia University in 2009.

Michael Eido Luetchford is a Buddhist studies author and philosopher. He studied electronic engineering at the University of Bradford (~1963–1967), studied under traditional teacher Gudō Wafu Nishijima (~1977–2007), and founded Windbell Publications.

Michael Friedrich is a Sinologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich (~1974–1984). He worked as an assistant at Munich (1983–1986) and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.
Michael Gregory Morony is a historian of the Near East and Central Asia. He earned his BA at UC Berkeley (~1957–1962) and MA at UCLA (~1962–1965), where he became a professor in 1974.

Michael Hahn was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau (PhD 1967). He held academic posts at the University of Bonn (1972–1988) and Marburg (visiting 1976–1980; chair 1988–2007).

Michael Hookham is a practitioner and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa (starting 1965) and Dilgo Khyentse, and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at SOAS and University College London. He held several posts at SOAS, including Head of the South Asia Department (1995–1999) and Associate Dean (2002–2010).
